candidates.name: Saint Clement of Ohrid Cathedral

candidates.name: Matka Canyon

candidates.name: Church of Saint George
candidates.content: Formerly the main church of the village, Saint George is one of a pair of 16th-century churches in Radišani. Its frescoes were originally painted in 1631.

candidates.alt: Црква „Св. Архангели Михаил и Гаврил“ - Кучевиште

candidates.name: Clock Tower

candidates.name: Church of the Holy Saviour

candidates.content: The Kurşumli Han (Turkish for "Lead Inn") is the largest and the most beautiful of the three remaining Ottoman caravansaries. It was built in 1550 by Mula Musledin Hoca, the son of a scientist on the court of Sultan Selim II. Both

candidates.name: Museum of Macedonia

candidates.content: The Çifte Hamam (Turkish for "double bath") was built in the middle of the 15th century by Isa Bey Ishaković. It was used as both a male and female bath, but unlike Daut Pasha Hamam where both parts go parallel to each other, here

candidates.name: Millennium Cross Cable Car

candidates.name: Church of Saint Nicholas
candidates.content: This smaller 16th-century church contains fragments of its original frescoes dating from 1631.

candidates.name: Skopje Fortress

candidates.name: Mustafa Pasha Mosque
candidates.content: Standing on a plateau above the Old Bazaar, this mosque is one of the most beautiful Islamic buildings in Macedonia. It was built in 1492 by Mustafa Pasha, vizier on the court of Sultan Selim I. The mosque is elegant and intact; n

candidates.name: Remains of Skupi

candidates.name: Macedonian National Theatre

candidates.name: Macedonia Square

candidates.name: Art Bridge
candidates.content: A pedestrian bridge across the Vardar, the Art Bridge runs from the cafes east of Macedonia Square to the Financial Police Building. The bridge contains 29 sculptures of noted North Macedonian musicians and artists.

candidates.name: Parliament Building

candidates.name: Philip II Arena
candidates.content: The largest stadium in the country with a capacity of over 33,000. Mostly used for football, it is home to FK Vardar and FK Rabotnički (both in the Macedonian First League) and the North Macedonia national football team. It first

candidates.name: Boris Trajkovski Sports Center
candidates.content: A modern arena home to the Macedonian national basketball, handball, and volleyball teams for both men and women. It also hosts concerts. Its maximum capacity is 8,000 for sports events.

candidates.name: Skopje Summer Festival

candidates.name: Offest
candidates.content: This festival takes place at several locations in Skopje, such as the Universal Hall, Skopje Square, the Youth Cultural Center, and many attractive night clubs in the city.

candidates.name: Skopje Jazz Festival
candidates.content: For one week every October, Skopje hosts eminent jazz musicians from all over the world. The Skopje Jazz Festival is considered to be one of the best of its kind in Europe.

candidates.name: May Opera Evenings
candidates.content: The May Opera Evenings have been one of the most visited events in Skopje. Over the years, the stage of the Macedonian Ballet and Opera Theatre has hosted a number of ballet performances, operas, and many concerts. This event repr

candidates.name: Autumn Music

candidates.name: Herdelezi / Djurdjevden
candidates.content: Spring festival celebrated at home and in public. Usually crowned by a great open air concert. After Herdelezi the wedding season begins. Almost every day you can meet a wedding procession or a procession accompanying the gifts fo

candidates.name: BuskerFest
candidates.content: Street performers festival. Tours Macedonian cities, as well as Budva, Montenegro and Sibenik, Croatia.

candidates.name: Taksirat Festival
candidates.content: One of the biggest winter festivals in Eastern Europe, which happens at the end of November and beginning of December.

candidates.name: Skopje Walks
candidates.content: A "free" walking tour of the major sites in Centar and the Old Town. The tour lasts about 3 hours.

candidates.name: City Park

candidates.name: Macedonian Philharmonic
candidates.content: Part of the Skopje 2014 project, but notable for having bold modern architecture instead of neoclassical. It was built to have excellent acoustics and features concerts regularly.

candidates.name: Walk the Vardar Quay
candidates.content: The quay runs from Park Aerodom at ASNOM and Kiro Gligorov boulevards in the east down to Centar in the west. Portions east of Park Aerodrom are under construction. Along the quay are bike lanes, walking lanes, pull-up and push-up

candidates.name: Katlanovo Baths
candidates.content: One of Macedonia's most popular bath centers. Located above Katlanovo on the Pčinja River, the healing waters have been used since Roman times. A hotel was first placed at the site in 1934 and is now visited by 10,000 guests annua

candidates.name: Explore Skopska Crna Gora
candidates.content: Meaning "Black Mountain of Skopje". Even though Vodno is the most popular hiking option in Skopje, a fun and educational day trip from Skopje is visiting the villages, churches and monasteries on Skopska Crna Gora Mountain. Easies

candidates.name: Stroll through the town
candidates.content: You can get a good first impression of the city's sights in one or two hours, covering bazaar, fort and post-earthquake buildings. Equipped with a guidebook and a city map you can easily do it on your own.

candidates.name: Beautiful City
candidates.content: A nice graffiti wall.

candidates.name: Vino Skop
candidates.content: Wine tasting, vineyard visits, live musical entertainment from international artists in the heart of the city.

candidates.name: Pivolend
candidates.content: Gourmet weekend with beer.

candidates.name: Hotel Arka

candidates.name: Intermezzo Music Bar
candidates.content: A cocktail bar.

candidates.name: Piazza Liberta
candidates.content: Eat the peanuts and throw the shells on the floor.

candidates.name: Nano Bar
candidates.content: Coffee, drinks, cocktails. LGBT friendly.

candidates.name: Rock bar „Old School“
candidates.content: Popular rock bar, considered among the best in the country.

candidates.name: Macedonian Pub DZE
candidates.content: New popular bar with young locals, not posh, but friendly.

candidates.name: Van Gogh Bar
candidates.content: Decent bar and restaurant, sociable atmosphere.

candidates.name: Bar Pogon
candidates.content: Chill and open air bar and coffee place.

candidates.name: Rock Bar Krug
candidates.content: A genuine neighborhood rock bar rather than a touristy night life spot.

candidates.name: VOX Night Club
candidates.content: In Karpoš. A nightclub usually crowded on weekends.

candidates.name: Pivnica Star Grad
candidates.content: Live music and homemade beer. It also serves some small plates.

candidates.name: Izzi Caffe
candidates.content: Cool place to have a drink, in the morning (coffee) or at night. The owner speaks English and will hang out with you to make sure you're taken care of.

candidates.name: Restaurant Old House

candidates.name: Restaurant Skopski Merak
candidates.content: Classic Macedonian restaurant with live music, grilled meats and extensive local wine selection. One of the best-known traditional restaurants in Skopje.

candidates.name: Pelister

candidates.name: Destan
candidates.content: Budget traditional ćevapi and kebab restaurant popular with locals and visitors. Fast, casual and focused on grilled meat dishes.

candidates.name: Dukat
candidates.content: Traditional-style Macedonian restaurant known for grilled meats, large portions and garden-style atmosphere.

candidates.name: Dva Elena Restaurant
candidates.content: Splurge Macedonian restaurant with extensive wine cellar and refined presentation of traditional dishes.

candidates.name: Restoran Aleksandrija 14
candidates.content: A few minutes drive away from the cent of the city. Beside the traditional Macedonian food, macrobiotic and vegetarian dishes are available for the guests.

candidates.name: Kaj Гоце
candidates.price: Main course + vegetables + beer + mastika = under 1000 denars
candidates.content: Traditional Balkan food.

candidates.name: Dropstop Gastrobar
candidates.content: Modern wine-focused gastrobar specializing in Macedonian wines, charcuterie and tasting menus with wine pairings. Located inside a modernist building from the Kingdom of Yugoslavia period that survived the 1963 Skopje earthquake.

candidates.name: Uranija
candidates.content: Recognized as one of the best restaurants in North Macedonia for more than a decade. Nice selection of local wine and food. Free Wi-Fi

candidates.name: Skopski Merak
candidates.content: Known for its traditional cuisine, wines, and rakija (brandy).

candidates.name: Gurmet
candidates.content: Traditional cuisine.

candidates.name: Super Vero

candidates.name: Green Market
candidates.content: An authentic farmers market less overrun by tourists and therefore much more decent prices and stall personnel. You can also find homemade spirits here and a few other shops.

candidates.name: Biser

candidates.name: Old Bazaar

candidates.name: Bit Pazar

Church of Saint Nicholas: This smaller 16th-century church contains fragments of its original frescoes dating from 1631.

Church of Saint Nicholas: The predecessor church here was built around the time of the Yahya Pasha Mosque in the Old Bazaar with permission to build granted by Yahya Pasha. The current church was built in 1881 and its frescoes were done the same year by Dičo Zograf.

Ljubanci Monastery: Reached via a narrow paved road above the village is this 19th century monastery. It was a home to monks before it became home to nuns in 1998. The monastery contains one church dedicated to Saint Nicholas, along with dormitories and a bell tower.

Church of Saint Nicholas Nikolimuki: Located just 300 m before Marko's Monastery is this small medieval church. Its date of construction is unknown but, based on the preserved portions of frescoes, it likely dates from the 13th or 14th centuries.
